/-!
# Erdős Problem 532

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/532](https://www.erdosproblems.com/532)
- [Er73] Erdős, P., *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory*. A survey of combinatorial theory (1973), 117-138.
- [Er75b] Erdős, Paul, *Problems and results in combinatorial number theory*. Journées Arithmétiques de Bordeaux (1975), 295-310.
- [Er77c] Erdős, Paul, *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III*. Number theory day (1977), 43-72.
- [Hi74] Hindman, Neil, *Finite sums from sequences within cells of a partition of $\mathbb{N}$*. J. Combinatorial Theory Ser. A (1974), 1-11.
-/

namespace Erdos532

/--
If $\mathbb{N}$ is 2-coloured then is there some infinite set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that
all finite subset sums$$ \sum_{n\in S}n$$(as $S$ ranges over all non-empty finite subsets of $A$)
are monochromatic?

Asked by Graham and Rothschild. Proved by Hindman [Hi74] (for any number of colours).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos532.lean"]
theorem erdos_532 :
    answer(True) ↔ ∀ (c : ℕ → Fin 2),
      ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧
        ∃ color : Fin 2,
          ∀ S : Finset ℕ, S.Nonempty → ↑S ⊆ A →
            c (∑ n ∈ S, n) = color := by
  sorry

end Erdos532

reformulations.difference: Er73 and Er75b use an infinite increasing sequence and nontrivial finite sums with coefficients in {0,1}. Lean uses an infinite set of naturals and sums over its nonempty finite subsets, without explicitly excluding zero from the set.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Remove zero from a witnessing set; it remains infinite and retains the monochromatic-sums property. Increasingly enumerate the remaining set. Injectivity makes sums over finite sets of indices equal the corresponding subset sums. Conversely, an increasing sequence has infinite range, and every finite nonempty subset of its range comes from a finite nonempty set of indices. Such index sets correspond exactly to nonzero finitely supported {0,1}-coefficient choices. The per-colouring equivalence with a strictly increasing positive sequence, and its universally quantified answer form, were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean as Review532.set_sequence_equiv and Review532.source_sequence_answer_equiv, without sorryAx.

review.notes: The sole declaration faithfully states the question in Er73 p. 122; Er75b p. 305 explicitly records Hindman’s affirmative solution. Quantifier scope, the uniform colour, distinct summands, nonempty subsets, and infinitude all check out. Boundary computations and equivalence proofs compile successfully. A scratch copy of the linked proof compiles against local Lean 4.33.1 after two unfolding-only Stream' compatibility edits, with axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. The live erdosproblems.com page returned a Cloudflare challenge despite descriptive User-Agent headers, and the full texts of Hi74 and Er77c were unavailable. The other cited primary sources suffice to settle the declaration’s faithfulness; the current community database confirms its recorded status.
